post.description:
Creates an account and emails a 6-digit verification code. No tokens are issued until the email is verified: call `POST /auth/verify-email` next.

- `accountType`: `customer` (default) or `vendor`. Admins cannot sign up.
- Guests sign up at checkout as customers; after verifying, merge the browser cart with `POST /cart/merge`.
- Vendors start with a business profile in `draft`; they turn on 2FA, complete `/vendor/profile`, upload documents and submit for verification.
- Signing up again with an email held by an **unverified** account replaces that account. A **verified** account is never replaced and returns 409.
- Rate limited: 5 requests burst, then one every 12 seconds, per IP.

post.description:
Confirms the 6-digit code emailed at signup and returns the first token pair, so the user is signed in straight away. Vendors get `twoFactorSetupRequired: true`: set up 2FA next.

- The code expires after `otpExpiresInSeconds` (default 10 minutes) and works once.
- Five wrong attempts burn the code; request a new one with `POST /auth/resend-otp`.
- Rate limited: 5 requests burst, then one every 12 seconds, per IP.

400.description: Body failed validation, or the code is wrong, expired or already used. All three look the same on purpose.

429.description: Rate limit hit. Honour the `Retry-After` header before retrying.

post.description:
Issues a new verification code for an account that has not verified yet, replacing the old one.

- Always answers 200 with the same shape, whether or not the email exists or is already verified, so it does not reveal accounts.
- One code per `resendAfterSeconds` (60). Asking sooner returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
- Rate limited: 3 requests burst, then one per minute, per IP.

429.description: A code was issued less than `resendAfterSeconds` ago, or the per-IP limit was hit. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

post.description:
Emails a 6-digit reset code to a **verified** account. Finish with `POST /auth/reset-password`.

- Always answers 200 with the same shape, whether or not the account exists.
- A reset code cannot be used as a signup code, or the reverse.
- One code per `resendAfterSeconds` (60); asking sooner returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
- Rate limited: 3 requests burst, then one per minute, per IP.

post.description:
Sets a new password using the code from `POST /auth/forgot-password`. New admins also use this, with the code from their welcome email.

- **Signs out every session** of the account, including access tokens already issued. The user signs in again with the new password.
- Two-factor sign-in stays on: the authenticator code is still needed. A user who lost their authenticator asks an admin to reset 2FA.
- Five wrong attempts burn the code.
- Rate limited: 5 requests burst, then one every 12 seconds, per IP.

post.description:
Checks email and password. Every account type signs in here; `role` tells the client which area to open.

- **Without 2FA**: `mfaRequired: false` plus the token pair.
- **With 2FA**: `mfaRequired: true` and an `mfaToken` (5 minutes), no tokens yet. Send it with the authenticator code to `POST /auth/login/2fa`.
- A vendor or admin who has not set up 2FA yet gets tokens with `twoFactorSetupRequired: true`; until 2FA is on, only `/auth/me`, `/auth/2fa/*` and sign-out work.
- Suspended accounts get 403 `Account suspended`; unverified emails get 403 `Email not verified`.
- Wrong email and wrong password return the same 401.
- Rate limited: 5 requests burst, then one every 12 seconds, per IP.

403.description: The password is right but the email is not verified yet (`Email not verified`), or an admin suspended the account (`Account suspended`).

429.description: Rate limit hit. Honour the `Retry-After` header before retrying.

post.description:
Second step for accounts with 2FA. Returns the token pair with `mfa: true`.

- Each code works once. An `mfaToken` dies after 5 minutes or when the password changes.
- Rate limited: 5 requests burst, then one every 12 seconds, per IP.

post.description:
Trades a refresh token for a new access token and a **new refresh token**. Each refresh token works once.

- Replaying a token that was already used is treated as theft: the whole session (every token descended from that login) is revoked and the call returns 401.
- Call this when the access token expires (`expiresIn` seconds after issue) or a protected route returns 401.
- Rate limited: 10 requests burst, then one every 6 seconds, per IP.

Always returns 204 with no body, even for an unknown or already-revoked token.

Rate limited: 10 requests burst, then one every 6 seconds, per IP.

info.title: fysi API
info.description:
REST API for Fysi, a marketplace for certified eco-friendly products with payments settled in USDC on Stellar. Verified vendors list products; customers browse and keep a cart without an account, then sign up to buy; admins verify vendors and moderate the catalogue.

**Machine-readable spec.** The OpenAPI JSON is served at `/docs-json`; feed it to a client generator for typed requests.

**Responses.** Every success is `{ statusCode, message, data }`. Paginated lists put `{ result, paginationMeta }` in `data`. Errors are `{ statusCode, message, data: null, error: { code, details, requestId, traceId, timestamp, path } }`. Validation errors list each problem in `error.details`.

**Money.** Prices are US dollars as integer **cents** (`priceCents: 1250` = $12.50); responses add a dollar string. Payment is 1:1 in USDC on Stellar, so there is no exchange rate. No floats.

**Sign-up and sign-in.** `POST /api/v1/auth/register` (`accountType` customer or vendor), confirm the emailed code at `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email` to get tokens, then send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Refresh tokens are single use: swap them at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`.

**Two-factor sign-in.** Vendors and admins must turn on an authenticator app (`/auth/2fa/setup` then `/auth/2fa/enable`); until then every other route answers 403 `Turn on two-factor sign-in to continue`. With 2FA on, `POST /auth/login` returns an `mfaToken` to finish at `POST /auth/login/2fa`.

**Admins.** No sign-up: the first super admin is created on the server with `pnpm admin:create`; super admins add admins with `POST /api/v1/admin/users`. Admin sessions idle out after `ADMIN_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`. Every admin action goes to the append-only audit log (`GET /api/v1/audit-logs`).

**Rate limits.** Every route has a per-client limit; sign-in and code routes have a stricter one. A 429 carries a `Retry-After` header in seconds.
